implementation_notes: Python's module is the singleton: a module is imported once and cached in sys.modules, so binding the instance to a module-level name - or hiding the state behind module functions - gives one shared instance with an obvious access point, and no __new__ guard, metaclass or getInstance() is needed. The class stays constructible, so keep it private by convention (underscore name) and export only the instance or the accessors. For lazy creation, decorate a zero-argument factory with functools.cache (3.9+) or functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None); the cache is thread-safe, though two threads racing the first call can both run the factory.
pitfalls: importlib.reload(), a second import path (the same file reachable under two names), namespace packages, or two installed copies of the distribution create a second module object and therefore a second 'singleton'.
Nothing enforces uniqueness: clients can still call the class constructor, so the pattern rests on the private-by-convention name and on review.

A module-level instance is created at import time (eager): expensive construction, file or socket access at import, or a cyclic import turns the cost into a startup problem - use a cached factory to defer it.
forked or multiprocessing children and subinterpreters each get their own copy of the module state.

variants.name: functools.cache factory function
variants.implementation_notes: The lazily initialised and testable form most Python code should prefer: a zero-argument factory decorated with functools.cache builds the instance on the first call and returns the cached one afterwards, so access goes through a callable seam that tests can reset with get_config.cache_clear(). The cache is thread-safe, but concurrent first calls may run the factory more than once and discard all but one result; use an explicit lock if constructing twice is harmful. On Python 3.8 use functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None).
pitfalls: The wrapped function can run more than once if another thread calls before the first call has been cached: guard side-effectful construction with a lock.
The factory must take no arguments, or only hashable stable ones; an argument-dependent factory is a cache/multiton, not a singleton.
cache_clear() is a public test seam - production code that depends on resetting it has smuggled the mutable global back in.
